debate.magnus: Alright, look, Brazil's the top dog, plain and simple. Always have been, always will be. But this Neymar business? He's out, not even travelling with the squad for matches. That’s a big hole in the lineup, a real gut punch. I remember '98, when Ronaldo wasn't 100%, and Brazil just wasn't the same. It changes the whole dynamic, makes a team play timid. On the other side, Norway's got Haaland, a proper beast, a legitimate threat to anyone, even the Brazilians. This is a knockout game, no room for lazy play, no sitting back. My big question is always, "Is the better team actually showing up today?" On paper, Brazil is, but without their main man, there's always a doubt. If they come out complacent, Norway could spring a surprise.
